featured_reviews.review_text:
When u walk along a promenade, distance covered is not important. Important is night colors capture along the Bay of Mahim shore in 1.25 km stretch. BWSL Promenede is a place placed beautifully on the way joining Western Mumbai to Southern Mumbai through magnificent Bandra Worli Sea Link (BWSL). While going to South Mumbai in morning or evening, just take a detour down below on left side before BWSL toll gate n u will be at Promenede on right side adjacent to Asha Bhosle Sargam Udyan. The promenade park opens/ closes at 06-09 a.m. n 05-09 p.m.
Attractive for Joggers, Runners, kids, elderly ppl, romantic couple, broken hearts n photo enthusiasts equally which I m proving thru pics. In this two level park stretch, there r three children parks of different age kids, four animals statues,  two public gyms. two amphitheaters, one basket ball court, uncountable romance sheds n endless retention wall n yes- no toilets.
There r two Balconies protruded in sea, beautiful dates tree witnessing dating couples on retention walls, park curves n geometry, artificial lit trees, beautiful imperial design poles of solar street lightings.
Found this park most beautiful in nights, especially at low tide times when u can see muddy land in various shapes representing a different natural profile in the sea from Meethi River Eastern side. And in the residual waters, beautiful light reflections in sea of Mahim- Dadar-Prabhadevi-Worli side high rise buildings lights.
Don't forget to see marvellous lighting decorations in this promenede from Christmas to Sankranti festival in mid January, which takes this already beautiful park to a totally different level.

Bandra Station is one of Mumbai’s most important stations connecting both the Western Line and the Harbour Line. It’s always crowded but trains are frequent so you don’t have to wait long.

The biggest advantage is its location. It’s the closest major station for places like Bandra Bandstand, Carter Road, Linking Road, Hill Road and the trendy cafes and shopping spots in the area. Autos and buses are easily available right outside.

The station itself is old but functional. Platforms are wide, indicators work well and foot-over bridges help manage the rush. It can get packed during peak office hours so plan accordingly.

If you're exploring Bandra or switching between Harbour and Western lines, this station is super convenient. Despite the rush, it’s one of the best connected stations in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Shekhar Kulkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bandra Railway Station is one of the most important and busiest railway stations in Mumbai, connecting thousands of commuters every day. I recently passed through the station and found it to be well-connected and convenient for both local and long-distance travelers. The station provides easy access to different parts of Mumbai through the Western Railway suburban network, making daily travel much more manageable.

The platforms are generally well maintained, and there are adequate facilities such as ticket counters, digital display boards, waiting areas, drinking water points, and food stalls. The station is also connected to nearby bus services, auto-rickshaws, and taxis, making onward travel convenient. Security personnel and railway staff are usually present to assist passengers and maintain order.

One of the biggest advantages of Bandra Station is its strategic location. It serves as a gateway to many popular areas of Mumbai, including Bandra West, Bandra East, Linking Road, and the Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC). The station is surrounded by shops, restaurants, and other essential services, which adds to its convenience.

Like most major stations in Mumbai, it can get extremely crowded during peak hours, and navigating through the station may sometimes take time. However, considering the large volume of passengers it handles daily, the overall management is quite efficient. Overall, Bandra Railway Station is a reliable, accessible, and essential transport hub that plays a vital role in Mumbai's public transportation network.

featured_reviews.name: Raghvendra Pathak
featured_reviews.review_text:
⚠️ WARNING: A True Horror Story on the Mumbai Local Train ⚠️
I have a story to tell, and I need every single person who romanticizes Mumbai to hear it. This isn't a cautionary tale; it's a terrifying account of a city that utterly failed me, proving that its glittering facade hides a dark, lawless reality.
My journey was supposed to be simple: my very first time on the legendary Mumbai Local Train, traveling from Naigaon Station to Bandra Station. I was looking forward to the authentic Mumbai experience. Instead, what I got was an experience of sheer terror and disgust that has permanently soured my view of this so-called "Financial Capital."
The moment the train moved, the compartment was seized by chaos. A group of about five young men—I can only describe them as uneducated, aggressive hooligans—were on board. They weren't just talking loudly; they were screaming, shouting obscenities, and creating a deafening, terrifying scene. The environment instantly turned hostile.
Then, the unthinkable happened. Their aggression boiled over, and these morons didn't just fight among themselves; they turned on an innocent co-passenger. Right there, in that cramped, moving metal box, one of them slapped a fellow traveler with shocking force. I was frozen. Everyone was frozen. The helplessness of being trapped with violent, out-of-control people while the train hurtled through the city was overwhelming.

I cannot emphasize this enough: Based on my deeply scarring experience, I strongly recommend that you reconsider traveling to Mumbai. If they can't manage basic safety on their most essential transport, they don't deserve your tourism, your business, or your respect. Save yourself the trauma. This city is not what the stories claim it is.

featured_reviews.name: Madhavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bandra Railway Station is one of Mumbai’s busiest and most important suburban stations, and it truly feels like the heart of the city in motion. Constantly buzzing with commuters, vendors, announcements, and trains, it captures the fast-paced spirit Mumbai is known for.

The station is well connected, serving both the Western and Harbour lines, which makes it a major interchange point and extremely convenient for daily travelers. Platforms are generally easy to navigate, and signage has improved over the years, helping even first-time visitors find their way around. The FOBs (foot over bridges) are wide and functional, though they can get very crowded during peak hours.

Cleanliness is decent by Mumbai local standards, but during rush hours the station can feel overwhelming. Crowd management remains a challenge, especially during office hours, when platforms and entrances become packed. Security presence is noticeable, which adds a sense of safety despite the chaos.

Outside the station, Bandra offers quick access to buses, autos, taxis, and the lively streets of East and West Bandra. Food stalls, small shops, and local vendors make it easy to grab a quick snack or essentials on the go.

Overall, Bandra Railway Station isn’t about comfort or calm—it’s about efficiency and connectivity. If you’re a regular commuter, it’s a lifeline. If you’re new, it’s an experience that introduces you to the real rhythm of Mumbai: crowded, loud, a bit messy, but always moving.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

featured_reviews.review_text: Thanks to Bombay Walks Mumbay became the highlight of my India trip! featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been with the group thrice so far. 2 walks and one trip. Have had the best experience everytime.
My recent trip was to Spiti valley.
First things first , the group is eco conscious. This is one of the most important factors behind my decision to go on trips with them.

Cheers 🤘🏻

featured_reviews.name: Goretti Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text: Being my first trek at the age of 50 I was not sure if I should go ahead with it, but Mr. Sandesh Lad assured that I would be fine and trek trained Ms. Tejasvi would take good care of us. His assuring words turned truth when Mr. Chandrakant (Pappu) and Ms. Tejasvi ensured that I was comfortable through the Trek as I had to take longer breaks because of steep stone paths and some patches of steep climb. I am glad I trusted Mr. Lad as the view up there was breath taking, fresh air and night halt in one of the ancient caves was amazing. The group was well looked after and the highlight was having traditional local dinner, breakfast and lunch in mud houses sitting on cowdung floors in the houses of locals. It was the best experience for me and I look forward to many more such experiences with " Let's go Outdoors". Very economical for the pocket too. Thank you Mr. Lad, Ms. Tejasvi and Mr. Chandrakant (Mr. Pappu).

featured_reviews.review_text:

The highlight of our trip was watching the turtles, which was a unique and memorable experience. Additionally, the food was amazing, as we had the opportunity to try delicious Maharashtrian cuisine.

featured_reviews.name: Rachana Thakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
HEAVEN FOR REAL #Letsgo

14/12/2017-17/12/2017
The best decision of joining the Digital Detoxification trip by Let’s Go Outdoors
I never knew that such a beautiful world exists until I decided to go for digital detox with let's go and explored the mesmerizing beauties of nature.
My first ever trip.
Uttarakhand,Jim Corbett

Meeting a group of unknown people who are no more unknown to me.
Traveling on beautiful roads of Delhi to Uttarakhand.
Reaching Jim Corbett and then walking towards Eco Resort for 45mins brought butterflies in my stomach of every surprise on the way. Crossing the river on a small raft made me happy like a kid.
Cool breeze hitting my face,sound of the river and birds made me feel so close to the nature. There I see the beautiful place where we will stay in the middle  of the forest welcoming me with wide open arms to experience the most amazing next 2days of my life.
Never thought mornings can be so beautiful in the forests and mountains where all you see is loving nature.
The lovely staff of the resort made us extremely happy by the service provided. The yummiest and healthy food they served and how can I forget the smiles on their faces after seeing us happy.
The experience of star gazing, bird watching, spotting animals like barking deer, sambar, lungurs, brown fish owl, vultures and many more. Sitting near the river side made me realise we are so unaware about our beautiful places and nature in our country. But not any more. I promised myself sitting near the river that I want to see more, learn more and LIVE MORE.
Today this is a ‘SUPER HAPPY ME’ after realising that we really must leave our phones and all the gadgets aside and live and enjoy the beautiful experiences, which cannot be captured by any camera of this world. It can only be felt.
In the end I am so grateful to Sandesh for taking me to such a beautiful place.
Memories for life☺

Elephanta Caves, a UNESCO site near Mumbai, features stunning 5th–7th century rock-cut temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. The Trimurti sculpture is a highlight.

Pros:
•	Rich history and intricate carvings
•	Scenic ferry ride from Gateway of India
•	Cultural and spiritual significance

Cons:
•	Some areas need better maintenance
•	Can get crowded with persistent vendors
•	Requires a ferry ride and a steep climb

Tips:
•	Visit early to avoid crowds
•	Wear comfortable shoes and carry water
•	Watch out for monkeys

A must-visit for history lovers and architecture enthusiasts!

featured_reviews.name: Anuradha Bhave
featured_reviews.review_text: When we say kokan, mostly beautiful beaches, and old style houses surrounded by coconut, mango, and cashew trees comes to everyone's mind. But the trip that we took with Girispandan was different in many ways. We got to experience a beautiful evening boat ride on a sangam point where 3 rivers met and witnessed the most beautiful evening sky displaying colour shades, which could not be captured by camera. The entire trip unfolded many aspects of the Kokan region with beautiful old temples, Katal Shilpa, Kashtha Shilpa museum, and amazing stay at Rai resort. This place truly lives up to its name, helping us experience what it's like to be one with nature and live in a place that is completely surrounded by endless trees and various species of birds. Last but not the least, the trip being Aamra Mahotsav, from the very first meal till the last we got to taste endless variety of Mango dishes and the actual naturally ripen mangoes along with many more other local culinary masterpieces that left us speechless. Many thanks to Girispandan  - Parag Dada and Bapat Sir and Mr. Amol and Mrs. Manek and their entire team from Rai resort for the greatest hospitality and an unforgettable experience. I'm looking forward to many more such trips with Girispandan.

featured_reviews.name: shruti kamble
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bandra Reclamation is truly one of the most refreshing spots in Mumbai to unwind and reconnect with nature. Whether you visit in the soft hues of the morning or during the calming golden hours of the evening, this place offers a peaceful escape from the city’s constant rush.

The open-air setting, with the gentle sea breeze and expansive sky, creates a soothing atmosphere that instantly lifts your mood. It’s perfect for leisurely walks, quiet moments of reflection, or simply enjoying the beauty of nature right in the heart of the city.

What makes it even more inviting is how thoughtfully the space is designed. There’s a small but convenient parking area, making access easy for visitors. Families will especially love the dedicated kids’ play area, complete with swings, seesaws, and spaces for physical activity where children can play freely and safely.

For those who prefer a slower pace, the seating areas are ideal to relax, read, or just watch the world go by. The walking paths are clean, well-maintained, and perfect for both morning fitness routines and evening strolls.

Overall, Bandra Reclamation stands out as a peaceful, clean, and beautifully maintained promenade—an ideal place to breathe fresh air, stay active, and enjoy simple moments close to nature. 🌿

featured_reviews.review_text: Great reclamation area perfect to take an evening strol, walk or jog while enjoying the nighttime city skyline, along with the love Mumbai sign and some amazing picture sports and great lighting. The view and the lights of the city skyline at night is great and exceptional. You can even see an amusement park in distant. Ample picnic tables and benches for rest. Some of them were shaded and some were unshaded. The wall along the sea line is a perfect spot to sit and spend a nice evening. Ample parking at the entrance. Overall, a highly recommended place to spend a nice evening in Mumbai. Check out videos and images and follow me for more detailed reviews

featured_reviews.review_text:
JAYA HE GVK NEW MUSEUM
Art and Culture : GVK CSMIA T2 is home to India’s largest public art programme, titled ‘Jaya He’, in the form of a 3.2 km multi-storey Art Wall, illuminated by skylights, that has over 5000 pieces of artwork and artifacts from every region & corner of India.
Possibly India’s largest public artwork project to date, Jaya He Museum at the Mumbai International Airport, spans across Terminal 2 and is a landmark corporate initiative to safeguard an immense cultural resource.

One of the few Installations I liked during my visit here:
1. Recycled & Unconventional Map of Mumbai
2.  Hawa Mahal in Turban denoting Vaayu (An element of panchmahabhuta)
3. Frozen Fire denoting Agni
4. Moving Constant- (Tanjore Paintings- Folk  Art Form)
5. Nomadic Tribes (Gadiya Lohar)
6. Vahanas (mount/vehicle) of a Hindu God
7. Palitana Painting (09/09/1934)
Special thanks to Ms.Ashwini Varma @ashwini_varma for a guided tour of the museum.
You can also plan your visit, for no matter how many times you transit through the airport, Domestic or International, it been created in a way that you will be see a new detail in these exquisite “narrative trails” rich in ethnographic stories every time you are at the Airport.
CSMIA gives you an opportunity to take a guided tour of the museum in the departures section. Called as Jaya He Safari, these tours can be availed for free as you depart from Terminal 2.

Jogger’s Park is one of Mumbai’s most beloved seaside urban parks and jogging spots, nestled at the southern end of Carter Road promenade in Bandra West. It’s a classic example of how community initiative transformed a former garbage dump into a green fitness haven in the early 1990s, thanks largely to local efforts led by Oliver Andrade and support from prominent Mumbai residents — a legacy memorialised by a plaque at the entrance that says “From Sir, With Love.”
Wikipedia

Park Highlights
Scenic jogging tracks: The park features a 400-metre long stretch with a mix of mud, synthetic and paved pathways that suit casual walkers and serious runners alike.

Sea views & fresh air: Its location along the Arabian Sea offers cool breezes and calming views of the water — especially beautiful at sunrise and sunset.
Chalbanjare
Green spaces & gardens: Beyond jogging, there are lush lawns, landscaped paths, benches and shaded spots perfect for relaxation, meditation, or reading.
Chalbanjare
Kid-friendly area: There’s a dedicated children’s play area with swings, slides and soft flooring, making it family-friendly.
The Indian Express

Activities & Atmosphere
Jogger’s Park isn’t just for fitness — it’s a community hub where locals gather for morning runs, evening walks, yoga sessions or simply to meet friends. It’s also known for hosting Mumbai’s first laughter club, a unique wellness activity that began here.

Visitors often enjoy:
Walking or running with sea views
Meditation and casual outdoor workouts
Relaxing on benches overlooking the coast
Family outings with kids in the play area

Practical Info
Timings: Typically open 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (best early morning and evening).
Whats Hot
Entry: Free to enter since the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) took over maintenance.  
Ticket Fairy

Ticket Fairy
Getting there: Easily reachable by auto/taxi from Bandra Railway Station, or by BEST buses along Carter Road.
Ticket Fairy

Jogger’s Park blends fitness with serenity a rare open space in a bustling city where you can breathe fresh sea air, watch waves crash, and enjoy a peaceful escape without leaving the suburb. Locals and visitors alike cherish it for its history, community vibe, and relaxed seaside ambience.
